response.working_thesis: The Harbor Lighting Ordinance set a wattage cap for new municipal walkway fixtures, and a limited pilot showed energy savings without addressing safety or cost concerns.
response.main_mechanism: The ordinance works by grandfathering existing fixtures while capping wattage only on new installations, so compliance builds gradually through natural replacement rather than mandatory retrofit. The pilot program tested this approach on a subset of fixtures and measured only electricity use, leaving other consequences of the policy unverified.

Section 4 requires municipal walkway fixtures installed after the effective date to be rated at no more than 20 watts.

The city council adopted the rule after a public hearing.
